narrative.overview:
UnpopularVoice is set like the front page of a serious newspaper running an investigation. A black masthead, heavy serif headlines, white newsprint, and one red rule that says "this is the story." The numbers are the headlines: revenue and losses are set in the same display serif as the titles, large and black, so a reader can screenshot a figure and it still reads as reporting, not marketing.

Density is editorial, not dashboard. Article pages hold a single 760px reading column with generous vertical spacing; index pages open into a 1280px grid of quiet white cards. Drama comes from contrast (pure black panels interrupting white pages) rather than from color, gradients, or imagery. There is no photography in the system and no illustration; the figures and the type carry the page.

Red is the masthead ink. It marks the brand, the call to subscribe, and the eyebrow of a section. It never marks a loss. Losses and gains have their own semantic reds and greens, kept deliberately distinct from the brand.
keyCharacteristics: Serif display (Playfair Display) for headlines and every headline figure; sans (Inter) for prose, UI, and labels.
Black, white, and Auditor's Red as the identity; greys for structure; green and red only for data.
Short red accent bar (48px by 4px) as the recurring masthead mark above headlines and dark panels.
Black pull-out panels for the one line meant to be screenshotted.
Tiny uppercase tracked labels as the eyebrow vocabulary.
Flat surfaces; hairline borders do the structural work.

rules.name: The Masthead Ink Rule
rules.body: Auditor's Red is identity, never data. A loss figure in Auditor's Red is a bug; it must be Loss Red.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Brand red (#B22222, darker, brick) and loss red (#DC2626, brighter) must never sit adjacent as if interchangeable. If a reader could confuse "brand accent" with "this number is bad," change one of them.

rules.name: The Sign Rule
rules.body: Red and green describe a number, never a judgement about it. Red: a negative figure, or an unsigned rupee figure whose label's subject is a loss, deficit, burn or outflow. Green: an explicitly "+" figure, or an unsigned rupee figure whose label's subject is a profit. Everything else is black: revenue, costs, cash, borrowings, valuations, ratios, and sentences in table cells. A cost is not a loss; a narrowing loss is still red; a transition ("−₹44 → −₹20 Cr") takes the colour of where it ends. Components derive this in `lib/tone.ts` (KeyMetrics, ChartBlock, FinancialTable, VersusBlock, hero figures); articles never choose red or green, and losses are entered as negative numbers in chart data. Direction arrows stay neutral. Ratings and categories (EmployerScore chips, RealityScore, InsightBox types, timeline events) keep their own palettes because they are not numbers.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every piece of text clears 4.5:1 (3:1 for 24px+ bold) on its actual ground; axe runs across every sitemap URL before a deploy. On paper, the lightest text is gray-500 (#6B7280); gray-300/400 are for rules and borders only. On black, the faintest text is white at 60%, except pure separators ("·"), which carry `aria-hidden` and may stay at 30%. On a tinted surface (red-50 band, score-tinted cards), secondary text takes the foreground at 60% (`text-black/60`) or the surface's own deep hue, never gray-500. Amber, yellow and orange text use their -700 shades.

rules.name: The Dark Ground Rule
rules.body: Auditor's Red, Loss Red and Profit Green are tuned for paper and fall under 4.5:1 on black. `app/globals.css` lifts them automatically inside any `.bg-black` / `.bg-gray-900` ground: brand red to #EB6B6B, loss red to #F87171, profit green to #4ADE80 (all at least 4.9:1 on #000 to #1D2432), and returns them to paper values inside a light panel or pale chip nested in that ground. Write the normal classes (`text-brand-red`, `text-red-600`, `text-green-700`); never hand-pick a dark variant per component.

rules.name: The Monochrome Ground Rule
rules.body: Pages are black and white first. Color appears as a mark (bar, eyebrow, chip, value), never as a large tinted surface, with two exceptions: the pale newsletter band and the cream takeaway panel.

rules.name: The Figures Are Headlines Rule
rules.body: Any number the article is about is set in the display serif at Figure size or larger. Numbers in Inter are supporting data only.

rules.name: The Whisper Label Rule
rules.body: Eyebrows and captions are tiny, uppercase, widely tracked, and grey or red. They never compete with the serif above or below them.

rules.name: The Single Column Rule
rules.body: Article bodies never go multi-column. Comparison components (VersusBlock, SplitView) may split into two panes inside the column, and collapse to stacked panes below `sm`.

rules.name: The Inversion Over Shadow Rule
rules.body: To make something stand out, turn it black. Don't raise it.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Every link, button and summary a reader taps is at least 44px tall, site-wide, including footer links, "see all" links and the wordmark. Most readers arrive on a phone; a target they miss is a page they leave.

dos: **Do** put the 48px by 4px Auditor's Red bar above every page-level headline and at the top-left of dark panels.
**Do** set every headline figure in Playfair Display at Figure size or larger, with Gain Green or Loss Red only when the value carries a direction.
**Do** use Masthead Black panels for the single line the reader should remember, at most one or two per article.
**Do** keep article prose at 1.0625rem / 1.75 in Body Ink within the 760px column.
**Do** use tiny uppercase tracked labels (10px, 0.25em) for section eyebrows, and 11px card labels for company names and figure captions.
**Do** keep every tap target at least 44px tall and check every homepage change at 360px and 390px wide.
**Do** use the verdict triplets exactly (green / amber / red background, border, text) for Solid / Watch / Caution.
donts: **Don't** use Auditor's Red (#B22222) for a negative number; negatives are Loss Red (#DC2626).
**Don't** use em dashes anywhere in UI copy, labels, or placeholders; use a comma, or a hyphen for empty-value placeholders.
**Don't** add gradients, photography, illustration, or large tinted surfaces; contrast does the work.
**Don't** lift elements with heavy shadows; invert them to black instead.
**Don't** set article bodies in more than one column.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue for identity; Auditor's Red is the only brand color.
